title: Property of the selected finite upper bound
statement: Let $I$, $d$, $\prec$ and $u$ be as in [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. For every finite subset $F\subseteq I$, every $i\in F$ satisfies $i\leq u(F)$.

proof.text: Prove the stronger list assertion: for every finite list l, every accumulator a and every j in l, j ≤ foldl d a l. Use induction by appending a final element k. The empty list has no members. For l ++ [k], the fold is d(foldl d a l, k). An old member is bounded by foldl d a l by induction and hence by the new fold by the first upper-bound property of d and transitivity. The final element k is bounded by the second upper-bound property of d. Apply this assertion to the auxiliary-order sorted enumeration of F from [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]; Finset.mem_sort identifies its members with F. On the sorted enumeration the final element is the largest, so this implements the fixed-order insertion induction without separately removing maxima from finsets.

proof_origin.place: ## Proof; E5 formalization by induction on the sorted list, 2026-10-18

proof.text:
Induct on $F$. The empty case is vacuous. At an insertion step, the
selected $d(u(F),i)$ bounds both $u(F)$ and $i$; transitivity and the
induction hypothesis prove the assertion for all old and new elements.
